segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for November 8th, 2026.
We've got exciting updates on humanoid trials, parts sequencing, and the latest from Figure's robot colony.
Tune in for the rundown.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, HSR-ER-HR705!".
This report details the specifications and current status of the HR705, a wheeled industrial humanoid from Huashu Robot demonstrating developing humanoid capability.

The robot stands at one hundred seventy centimeters tall and weighs two hundred kilograms, incorporating two seven-degrees-of-freedom collaborative arms for factory tasks such as obstacle avoidance, sorting, and assembly.
The platform utilizes Laser SLAM navigation and vision cameras for industrial space movement and object interaction.
Skill scoring indicates a development level of three out of ten, with navigation capabilities rated lower than manipulation skills.
Furthermore, the robot offers industrial connectivity through EtherCAT and Modbus protocols and is currently cataloged as a prototype.
This development signals ongoing progress in the integration of mobile robotics into industrial automation environments.
From Humanoid.guide, Audi humanoid robot trial targets parts sequencing in Ingolstadt.
This report details an experiment where wheeled humanoid robots are being tested at the Audi plant to pick and sequence vehicle parts using image recognition.
The system employs two arms to handle variously shaped and packaged components from containers, training the robots using both real and simulated images to manage variations in parts effectively.

This testing was designed to validate the reliable performance of the sequencing task within a logistics setting, involving collaboration between Audi, Agile Robots, Dassault Systèmes, and NVIDIA to address automation challenges.
The project focuses on proving the feasibility of advanced robotic manipulation in complex industrial environments.
This research indicates progress toward more robust and adaptable automation solutions in manufacturing and logistics.
From Humanoids Daily, "Figure’s HQ Is Crawling With Figure 03 Robots. What Are They All Doing?"
This report details the observation of numerous Figure 03 robots on the company campus and their current activities.

The company has built its one thousandth Figure 03, but customer deployments are limited, with most observed robots engaged in non-task activities such as walking or standing rather than performing paid work.
These robots are currently utilized for internal testing, data collection for Helix models, and ongoing experiments, indicating a movement toward a high density of robots on-site.
This development signals an increased focus on robotic presence within the development and testing environments of advanced artificial intelligence systems.
From The Robot Report, "Robot integration brings high-precision production to midmarket manufacturers".

This report details how the integration of robotic systems makes high-precision manufacturing accessible to midmarket and smaller manufacturers by offering lower costs, simplified programming, and enhanced capabilities through artificial intelligence and sensors.
Robotic systems enable these manufacturers to improve efficiency, alleviate labor shortages, and satisfy stringent quality requirements.

Real-world applications demonstrate robotics enhancing flexible production processes, including precise part marking, increased throughput, and automated bin picking across numerous industrial sectors.
Consequently, these robotic solutions facilitate sustainable growth for these manufacturers by rendering advanced precision techniques feasible.
The ongoing development of these technologies indicates a continued trend toward democratizing advanced manufacturing capabilities.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Standing in the way of slop bowls: the woman blocking food delivery robots".
This report details a protest action taken by a woman to assert public input regarding the presence of food delivery robots in public spaces.
The action occurred in Philadelphia where the individual physically obstructed the robots to raise awareness about the issue.
Supporters argued that the robots presented hazards and impacted employment, while others viewed the actions as controversial.
The incident reflected wider public skepticism concerning artificial intelligence and automation, prompting discussions about the role of these technologies in public infrastructure.
The event underscores the need for public consultation in determining the operational parameters for robotics in public settings.
This situation signals an ongoing debate regarding the integration and regulation of automated systems in communal environments.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, DH-5-6!".
This segment details the assessment of the DH-5-6 dexterous hand, which received a Humanoid Guide Hand Score of four out of ten, placing it in the developing performance range.
The assessment included a Degrees of Freedom rating of two out of five and a Strength rating of two out of five, indicating a balanced performance profile.

The evaluation process focused on application-specific evaluation, advising that prospective buyers should consider required movements and grip consequences before integration rather than relying solely on the aggregate score for demanding manipulation tasks.
The hand is manufactured by DH Robotics Technology Co., Ltd. and is listed at four thousand dollars.
Further evaluation of specific manipulation requirements is necessary for integration.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Xiao Di!".

This report details the development of Xiao Di, BYD's first self-developed humanoid robot designed for customer interaction in car dealerships and various applications, demonstrating emerging capabilities in navigation and manipulation.
The robot stands at 161 centimeters and weighs 58.5 kilograms, featuring a humanlike body with rounded joints and ten fingers.
Development is being conducted by BYD's embodied AI research team, focusing capabilities on obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly.
The prototype is currently valued at twenty-five thousand US dollars and is being developed to serve service, education, and industrial applications extending the automaker's work beyond vehicles.
This advancement indicates further exploration into embodied artificial intelligence for complex real-world tasks.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Centaur G1!".
This report details the specifications and capabilities of the Centaur G1, a wheeled humanoid robot designed for precision manufacturing environments.
The robot measures one hundred fifty centimeters in height and weighs two hundred sixty kilograms, possessing twenty degrees of freedom across its structure, two articulated arms, and a mobile base.
Key functionalities include obstacle avoidance and goods sorting, achieved through the utilization of camera sensors for perception and simultaneous localization and mapping navigation.
The system integrates Elite Robots' collaborative robot technology with an embodied artificial intelligence platform for control.
The robot is currently listed as in production with a price point of forty-eight thousand US dollars.
This development indicates continued advancement in the integration of embodied AI and mobile robotics within manufacturing settings.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Gino 1!".
This segment reports on the introduction of Gino 1, a wheeled humanoid robot designed for warehouse environments with specific capabilities in sorting and obstacle avoidance.

Gino 1 measures 168 centimeters and weighs 63 kilograms, featuring articulated arms equipped with tactile hands for navigating obstacles and sorting goods at a maximum speed of 5.4 kilometers per hour.
The robot's operation is powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor and the Geek+ Brain platform for its computing and control systems.
The assessment indicates a low Humanoid.Guide Skill Score, concentrating the robot's functionality on warehouse sorting tasks.
This launch occurred in February 2026 with a listed price of 55,000 US dollars.
The development signals ongoing advancements in practical robotics application within industrial logistics sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, DexHand021 S!".
This segment details the introduction of the DexHand021 S, a compact, three-finger robotic hand manufactured by DexRobot, noting its low cost and light weight.
The device weighs 0.6 kilograms and measures 208 by 80 by 82.8 millimeters, establishing it as an entry-level option priced at one thousand US dollars.
Performance evaluations place the hand in the developing category, exhibiting low ratings for both dexterity and strength.

The design prioritizes a simpler physical format compared to five-finger alternatives, and the product is currently in production pending further integration decisions based on specific task requirements.
This development indicates a push toward accessible, though currently limited, robotic manipulation tools.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, MagicHand H01!".
This report details the initial assessment of the MagicHand H01 robotic hand, which has received an overall Hand Score of five out of ten, indicating a developing product.

The assessment of the component ratings revealed four out of five for Degrees of Freedom and one out of five for Strength, suggesting a greater favorability in the dexterity aspects compared to the physical strength capabilities of the device.
The MagicHand H01 is currently in production and has a listed cost of fifteen thousand United States dollars.
This evaluation provides insight into the current developmental stage of advanced robotic manipulation technology.
Further developments in dexterity and strength metrics will be monitored within the robotics sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "XPeng IRON walks off automated line, targets 2026 production".
This report details the progress of the XPeng IRON humanoid robot, which has completed assembly and exited an automated production line, setting a target for mass production by the end of 2026.
The company reports that over eighty percent of core manufacturing processes for the robot are automated, adhering to automotive-grade quality standards.
The robot is equipped with seventy-six degrees of freedom and utilizes proprietary onboard artificial intelligence chips to execute autonomous tasks.
Funding is allocated to a commercial rollout plan beginning with internal deployments before a broader launch in 2027.
XPeng anticipates increased gross margins for these humanoid robots attributed to their inherent technical complexity.
This development indicates a tangible progression toward the commercialization of advanced humanoid robotics.
And that's all the circuits for today's digest.
Hope your day is as smoothly programmed as HSR-ER-HR705!
Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming.
Thanks for tuning in!
